definitions.explanation: A great ape native to Africa, known for its intelligence and close genetic relationship to humans.

examples.japanese: {動物園|どうぶつえん}でチンパンジーを{見|み}た。
examples.english: I saw chimpanzees at the zoo.

examples.japanese: チンパンジーは{道具|どうぐ}を{使|つか}うことができる。
チンパンジーは{人間|にんげん}に{最|もっと}も{近|ちか}い{動物|どうぶつ}の{一|ひと}つだ。
examples.english: Chimpanzees are one of the animals closest to humans.

notes:
SCIENTIFIC CLASSIFICATION:
チンパンジー belongs to the great ape family ({類人猿|るいじんえん}). The Japanese name comes from the English "chimpanzee."

RELATED VOCABULARY:
・ゴリラ (gorilla)
・オランウータン (orangutan)
・{類人猿|るいじんえん} (great ape)
・{霊長類|れいちょうるい} (primate)

FUN FACT:
Chimpanzees share approximately 98-99% of their DNA with humans, making them our closest living relatives along with bonobos (ボノボ).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・チンパンジーの{群|む}れ (a group of chimpanzees)
・チンパンジーを{飼育|しいく}する (to keep/raise chimpanzees)
・チンパンジーの{知能|ちのう} (chimpanzee intelligence)
